rebel-inc game sourced

Rebel Inc.

A counterinsurgency strategy game in which the player, as a coalition governor, spends a monthly budget on civilian and military initiatives to build popular support and stabilize regions of a war-torn country while corruption, inflation, and an insurgency push back.

2018Ndemic CreationsPolitical simcluster c048 mechanics
this record asyaml sourcemarkdownjson

core loop

fund civilian initiatives in regions -> popular support rises -> spending raises corruption and inflation -> an insurgency emerges and contests regions -> deploy troops, counter corruption, or negotiate -> stabilize the country to win

design notes

Rebel Inc. inverts Ndemic's earlier Plague Inc.: instead of spreading a disease, the player contains an insurgency by building popular support, and spending itself generates corruption and inflation. The tension is between civilian initiatives that win support slowly and military spending that holds ground without building support. Corruption as a side effect of spending is not yet a mechanic in the taxonomy (proposal corruption-leakage).

uses

Treasury and budget

A monthly budget funds infrastructure, jobs, education, roads, and military spending; the more initiatives the player funds, the more corruption and inflation rise, and the Economist governor receives the whole budget annually.

core
uses

Citizen satisfaction

Civilian initiatives raise popular support region by region, and stabilizing the country without letting insurgents take control is the goal.

core
uses

Stability and unrest

An insurgency emerges partway through and contests regions against coalition forces; later, peace can be negotiated with insurgent leaders.

core
uses

Corruption leakage

Funding more civilian initiatives raises corruption and inflation, which erode what the monthly budget achieves; the governance tab offers anti-corruption measures.

supporting
uses

Policy toggles

A governance tab offers anti-corruption measures.

supporting
uses

Scenario objectives

Each region has its own geography, and selectable governors such as the Economist and the Warlord change the rules.

supporting

Triggered event chains

Random events interrupt plans and offer choices.
